description:
Goal: collapse the dual-IR seam between Filament's substrate and its web backend. After this epic, vnode tuples are the only thing that crosses substrate→backend. `Reconciler.mount/3` and `Reconciler.update/4` return vnode trees; `~F` compiles to vnode-emitting code; the web backend owns the conversion from vnode tree to `%Phoenix.LiveView.Rendered{}` (preserving keyed-comprehension shape for PLV's diff engine).

Parent: flm-3wr.

## Why this first

The vnode↔`%Rendered{}` duality is the structural seam every other substrate decision in flm-3wr trips on. Sharpening this boundary makes Phases 2–5 local cleanup. Phase 2 (event handles tuple-shaped, capture/bubble dispatch), Phase 3 (cells), Phase 4 (module rename), Phase 5 (docs) are planned siblings; their decomposition waits until this phase's pattern is shaken out.

## Boundary that becomes sharp

- `Filament.Renderer.render/3` returns `{vnode_tree, new_hook_slots, pending_effects, new_fibers, new_event_handlers}` — no `%Rendered{}`.
- `Filament.Reconciler.mount/3` and `Reconciler.update/4` return vnode trees.
- `~F` produces vnode tuples (or a closure returning them); the existing AST passes (lexical scoping, auto-memoization, keyed-comprehension hoisting) are reframed for vnode-emitting bodies.
- `Filament.Web.RenderToRendered` (working name) converts vnode tree + fiber tree to `%Phoenix.LiveView.Rendered{}` with PLV-compatible keyed-comprehension shape and `phx-event="filament:..."` attribute rewrites.
- `Filament.LiveView` calls the converter once per render to feed PLV's diff engine.
- Substrate modules have zero references to `Phoenix.LiveView.*`.

## Out of scope (filed later as siblings)

- Phase 2: event handles tuple-shaped, capture/bubble dispatch, return-value protocol.
- Phase 3: cell mechanism with pluggable transports.
- Phase 4: module rename to `Filament.Web.*` namespace.
- Phase 5: documentation.

## Acceptance

- `mix test` (329+) passes.
- `mix credo --strict` and `mix dialyzer` clean.
- Examples (todo, cart, collaboration, inventory) interactive in Chrome; no console errors, no view crashes.
- `grep -r "Phoenix.LiveView" lib/filament/{reconciler,renderer,hooks,fiber,fiber_tree,render_context,vnode}.ex` returns nothing.
- Wire format inspected via WebSocket frames is byte-compatible (or smaller) for the todo example: keyed comprehensions still emit `"k"`/`"kc"`, fiber-id wire refs unchanged.

## Children

Sequence: 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.3 → 1.4 → 1.5.

- **1.1** Substrate vnode walker — split `render_vnode/2` into a substrate walker (registers fibers, returns vnode tree) and discard the HTML-emitting half.
- **1.2** `Renderer` + `Reconciler` return vnode tree — substrate signatures lose `%Rendered{}`. Transitional shim at LiveView boundary preserves behavior.
- **1.3** `Filament.Web` vnode→`%Rendered{}` converter — new module, owns HTML escape, `phx-event` rewrites, keyed-comprehension struct construction.
- **1.4** `~F` codegen target switch — `VNodeCompiler` produces vnode-emitting code; existing AST passes (lexical scoping, memoization, keyed-comprehension hoisting) reframed for vnodes.
- **1.5** LiveView wiring + examples + Chrome validation — converter wired into `Filament.LiveView`, transitional shim removed, examples Chrome-validated, substrate grep-clean.
title: [EPIC] Phase 1: vnode IR canonical, web converter at the boundary
